messages:
Sunita Rao: Quick heads-up — we need a coordinated plan for telemetry from Private/VPC/on-prem installs. Key constraints: many customers only allow outbound 443 through a NAT/proxy, strict firewall allowlists, and some require KMS/HSM-signed attestations/audit hooks. We also need new dashboard dimensions (deployment_mode + tenant labels) and runtime-vs-infra separation. Thoughts on connector architecture and security model?

Kevin Choi: +1. Proposal: a small metrics-agent running on the node that buffers telemetry and forwards to a signer-enabled forwarder inside the customer's VPC. That forwarder opens only outbound mTLS connections to collector.redwood.ai:443. Agent -> forwarder path can be local unix socket or localhost HTTP. Forwarder handles batching, chunking, and retries.

Olivia Martinez: Security notes: we must avoid sending raw customer identifiers without consent. For signing, we can support two modes: 1) customer-managed KMS (they sign payloads locally; we verify signature with pubkey) or 2) Redwood-signed tokens provisioned during install, with HSM-backed rotation. Either way, audit hooks should emit an entry for every exported batch: {cluster_id, time, signed_digest, signer_id}. Also need to document SLOs for retention of buffered telemetry on local disk.

Mike Liu: On the console/dashboard side: we need the following new labels for charts and rollouts: deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), tenant_scope (tenant|global), cluster_id, model_variant, route, and export_transport (direct|forwarder|s3-bundle). We should surface a telemetry-health panel per-customer that shows last-export-time, bytes/payloads dropped, and last-signature-verified. UX-wise the rollout page should show whether telemetry from a canary is actually arriving before we promote.

Dana Pratt: Firewall bit: many customers disallow outbound to arbitrary hosts — they prefer allowlist by domain or IP range. Recommend we provide a stable FQDN and set of IP ranges (and a DNS TTL guidance). Also we need to support HTTP proxy env vars and socket-level proxy (socks5) since some on-prem stacks funnel through internal egress proxies.

Kevin Choi: Implementation notes: use OTLP/HTTP for payloads (protobuf+json fallback). Batching window configurable (default 1s/2000events). If mTLS not possible, fallback to TLS + signed JWT in header: "X-Redwood-Signature: <base64(sig)>" and "Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token>". Example forwarder curl:

```
curl -v -X POST https://collector.redwood.ai/v1/telemetry \
  -H "Content-Type: application/protobuf" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=<sig>" \
  --data-binary @batch.pb
```

We should also support splitting large batches into chunked uploads (chunk-id + total-chunks headers) so we avoid large memory spikes.

Olivia Martinez: For KMS integration: support AWS KMS/EKSKMS, Google KMS, and PKCS#11 HSM for air-gapped installs. Key rotation must be auditable; prefer signed key-rotation events emitted to both customer audit log and our control plane (if allowed). Add support for per-tenant key metadata so ops can confirm which key signed which batch.

Sunita Rao: For dashboards we need two metric families: runtime_metrics (per-inference latency, token_count, kv_cache_hit_rate) and infra_metrics (cpu/gpu_util, mem, host_io). Runtime metrics should carry model_version and route labels; infra metrics should NOT carry PII tenant labels unless customer opts in. This will affect sampling and storage lifetime in infra.DBS.

Mike Liu: Agreed — add a "privacy_class" tag: pii_allowed|no_pii. Dashboard ingestion pipeline will route pii_allowed to longer retention and restricted viewers. Also need a new alert: telemetry-silence (no exports for >5m for a running cluster) and telemetry-degraded (error-rate > 1% over 1m).

Dana Pratt: Ops question: what about fully air-gapped installs that can't make outbound connections at all? We should support a pull model where customers export bundled signed files to a customer-managed S3 (or scp) and they provide a notification hook (webhook) or manual upload to our intake. But this is higher friction — document as optional flow.

Kevin Choi: Implementation checklist draft:
- metrics-agent binary (v0.1) with unix-socket + metrics buffering (owner: infra-agent)
- forwarder container + mTLS client cert support (owner: eng-infra)
- OTLP/HTTP protobuf support + chunking (owner: eng-runtime)
- KMS adapters (AWS/GCP/PKCS11) + rotation audit (owner: eng-security)
- dashboard labels + privacy_class routing + alerts (owner: eng-platform/console)
- docs + install playbook + allowlist IPs + DNS (owner: developer-experience)

deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-proposals/pull/341 — metrics-agent + forwarder spec.

audit-bot: Audit: key_rotation event recorded for install-template v2 at 2026-03-01T12:03:04Z (id: kr_78ab).

Sunita Rao: Can each owner ack and add ETA? Also need mapping of which metrics are considered high-sensitivity (can't leave local disk beyond 24h).

Kevin Choi: ack — infra-agent owns agent binary, ETA: prototype in 2 weeks, security review in 4.

Olivia Martinez: ack — KMS adapters ETA: initial AWS/GCP in 3 weeks, PKCS11 in 6 weeks. Will add sensitivity matrix to the PR.

Mike Liu: ack — dashboard schema PR by next sprint (10 business days). Will add telemetry-health tiles and telemetry-silence alert.

Dana Pratt: ack — ops doc + allowlist IPs published in 5 business days. Will include NAT/proxy examples and SOCKS5 notes.

Sunita Rao: Great — I'll consolidate the checklist into the PR and add action owners. If anyone has additional constraints (export throttles, quotas per-tenant, or legal redlines) drop them here before EOD. :+1:

Kevin Choi: One more note — we should throttle telemetry from heavy tenants client-side (token-bucket) and surface per-tenant quota usage to the console. Otherwise a single canary can blow our forwarder queues.

Olivia Martinez: Add: legal needs a short one-pager on what telemetry contains (no raw inputs, only derived counts and anonymized IDs unless opted-in). I'll loop in Legal.

Mike Liu: I'll add a small "telemetry status" badge in the rollout flow so engineers know if private telemetry is active during canary.

Kevin Choi: thanks — closing loop. I'll start the prototype.
